messages:
Ana (oncall): heads-up — we're getting a multi-customer spike of 500/503s hitting hosted inference since ~02:05 UTC. Dashboard shows a cluster of inference containers restarting in a short window (CrashLoopBackOff). Customers: two PLG accounts + 1 paid seat.

SRE-Bot: alert: hosted-inference-prod upstream_restarts > 15/min on pool-gpu-3 (metric threshold breached).

Diego: I'm on it. looking at kube events for pool-gpu-3 — seeing `OOMKilled` and `ContainerSandboxFailed` followed by `SIGSEGV` in container logs for a few pods. Pulling recent logs now.

Priya (support L2): cc @Ana — one customer opened a support ticket: their calls are failing with 503s and latency hitting 10s before error. They included a sample request and said it worked earlier today. Customer wants ETA.

Ana (oncall): thanks. Diego please share repro snippet if you can. Priya, can you ask customer for the prompt length + model + any recent config changes (e.g., max_tokens, streaming) while we triage?

Diego: log snippet from one crashed container: 
```
2026-03-15T02:06:12.345Z ERROR upstream: runtime error: CUDA out of memory. attempted to allocate 1.2 GiB
Traceback (most recent call last):
  File "inference_worker.py", line 412, in generate
    outputs = model.forward(inputs)
  File "torch/cuda/__init__.py", line 120, in _lazy_init
    raise RuntimeError('CUDA out of memory')
RuntimeError: CUDA out of memory
*** SIGSEGV (Segmentation fault) at 0x7ffc3b1dd000 ***
Container exit code: 137
```
Looks like a sequence: OOM then segfault then container killed.

Micah (infra): that pattern matches when driver memory desync occurs post-OOM — kernel panics or segfaults inside the GPU runtime sometimes follow. Are we running any recent model/quantization changes on that pool?

Diego: There's a recent config push last night that enabled dynamic kv-cache pre-allocation for certain Llama variants on pool-gpu-3. I rolled that out as a canary yesterday at 23:40Z.

Priya (support L2): customer says they sent a very long prompt (~120k chars) and bumped max_tokens to 16384. They didn't change model.

Ana (oncall): ok that aligns — long prompt + large max_tokens + kv prealloc could blow mem. Immediate mitigation ideas: 1) disable the kv prealloc config on pool-gpu-3 (roll back), 2) route traffic away from pool-gpu-3 to warm pool-gpu-1/2, 3) temporarily enable fallback to smaller model variant or CPU fallback for customers with extreme lengths. Micah, can you do routing? Diego, can you roll the kv change back?

Micah (infra): starting controlled drain of pool-gpu-3 now. We'll cordon nodes and set k8sPodEviction to drain with 1m grace. Also adding a routing rule to send new sessions to pool-gpu-1,2. Should push within 90s.

Diego: rolling back kv prealloc for the canary tag on pool-gpu-3 now. command: `kubectl set env deploy/inference --env KEYV_PREALLOC=false -n hosted-prod-pool-gpu-3` — applying.

SRE-Bot: deploy event: inference@hosted-prod-pool-gpu-3: KEYV_PREALLOC=false by diego.

Diego: after the rollback, restarted a few pods. watching logs — initial restarts look cleaner, no immediate segfaults. But I still see an OOM for one unusually large request (likely that 120k char prompt).

Priya (support L2): replied to customer with workaround: set max_tokens to 2048 and/or chunk the prompt. offered to route their traffic to a dedicated capacity if they need those extremes. Customer appreciated the quick workaround.

Ana (oncall): Micah — can we also add a temporary guard on request size at the API layer to prevent requests that will obviously blow memory? Even a soft-block returning 413 with guidance would help.

Micah (infra): yep. I can push a lightweight filter at the edge: if prompt length > 80k OR (prompt_len + max_tokens) > 100k, return 413 with message pointing to best practices. Pushing a fast feature flag now.

Diego: reproduction steps for devs: we reproduced locally by sending a single-shot request using the sample customer prompt with the older kv-prealloc enabled. Curl example: 
```
curl -sS -X POST "https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"model":"llama-xxl-canary","input":"<120k chars>","max_tokens":16384}'
```
That reliably triggers OOM + segfault in our canary under identical hardware.

Priya (support L2): capturing customer repro in support ticket 45231. Marking as escalated -> priority_support.

Ana (oncall): immediate status: routing change + kv rollback + edge guard deployed. Are errors dropping?

Micah (infra): monitoring: upstream_restarts on pool-gpu-3 dropped from 22/min to 2/min over last 4 minutes. API 5xx rate across hosted decreased by ~78% within 5 minutes.

Diego: one lingering pod showed a segfault during restart but subsequent pods are stable. I'll keep rolling restarts until all pods show green.

BillingBot: note — no billing spikes detected for affected customers in last 20 minutes. Charge events normal.

Priya (support L2): updated the customer: rolled back a platform change; recommended prompt splitting and lower max_tokens; offered a Dedicated trial if they need sustained very large context. Customer asked for a root cause writeup.

Ana (oncall): next steps: Diego to capture core dumps / stack traces from the crashing pods (if available) and open an infra bug for kv prealloc memory accounting. Micah to add the prompt-size guard to prod permanently until we have safe prealloc. Priya to coordinate customer comms + RC timeline. I'll schedule a postmortem meeting for 24h.

Diego: capturing cores now. here's the kernel log snippet showing driver complaint: 
```
Mar 15 02:06:13 worker-23 kernel: NVRM: Xid (PCI:0000:65:00): 79, GPU has fallen off the bus.
Mar 15 02:06:13 worker-23 kernel: NVRM: Xid (PCI:0000:65:00): 31, Ch 00000040 intr 10000000
```
That `GPU has fallen off the bus` lines correlate with the segfaults. saving to issue.

Micah (infra): saving current mitigation as runbook steps under incidents/1901004321. We'll also add an alert to detect kv-prealloc config toggles in canary pools.

Ana (oncall): thanks everyone. I'll post a short incident summary to #incidents after we confirm stability and then create a postmortem ticket. Good triage. :thumbsup:

Priya (support L2): noted. marking ticket 45231 as 'mitigated' and sending summary to customer with next-steps.

Diego: all pods in pool-gpu-3 are green now, no new 500/503s in last 7 minutes. will keep watch for 30m and then promote to resolved if stable.

SRE-Bot: incident_watch: stability OK. ongoing monitoring for 60m.

Ana (oncall): closing interim channel notes here. Postmortem owner: Diego. Postmortem ETA: 72h.
